solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Precious metal seen in swamp is an illusion

indicators.note: something seen in a place sits inside it, so the metal goes within the swamp word

parts.note: a mire is a swamp or bog
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A traveller glimpses silver glinting in a bog, but it turns out to be imaginary.
explanation.definitionFit: A desert vision of water that is not really there is the classic optical illusion.

clue.text: Flyers for service inspiring rector

indicators.note: inspiring literally means breathing in, so the service takes in the rector

parts.note: matins is morning prayer

explanation.surface: Birds fly over a church service that inspires its rector.
explanation.definitionFit: These are birds of the swallow family, so flyers by example.

clue.text: Push back about dessert one had

parts.note: re means about, concerning
pud is British slang for pudding, dessert
I is the Roman numeral one
ate means had, as a meal

explanation.surface: A diner refuses the pudding they had been served.
explanation.definitionFit: To repudiate is to reject or refuse, figuratively pushing a thing away.

clue.text: Greek flower game

parts.note: something that flows, a river: the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: A Greek flower used in some game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' means something that flows, a river, not a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Game here means wild birds hunted for sport, and this moorland bird is one.

clue.text: Cheer lab that constructs whitening mechanism

indicators.note: the letters of the preceding words are built into something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A cheerleading laboratory apparently builds devices for whitening things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that constructs' is the anagram signal: the letters of CHEER LAB are rebuilt.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that bleaches makes things whiter, so it is an agent or device for whitening.

clue.text: Unpleasant secretion wipes out second tree

indicators.note: the second's letter is wiped away from the secretion word

parts.note: slime is a nasty, sticky secretion

explanation.surface: A tree is cleaned of something nasty in a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: The linden is also called by this name, a common British tree.

clue.text: Showing body structure of a new type of bomb

parts.note: the atomic bomb is a kind of bomb

explanation.surface: A diagram showing the internal structure of a novel bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomy is the study of bodily structure, so this adjective means relating to it.

clue.text: Pester bishop to visit literary festival

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside, so the bishop goes within the festival

parts.note: the Hay Festival is held at Hay-on-Wye in Wales
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: Fans pester a bishop who is attending a book festival.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hay Festival is a famous British literary festival in Hay-on-Wye; bishops are styled Right Reverend, RR.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry is to harass or keep bothering someone.

clue.text: Again pulled prison guard up north

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read from the bottom, reversed

parts.note: a warder guards prisoners
N is north

explanation.surface: A prison guard was hauled up north once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawn means pulled, so drawn again is pulled again.

clue.text: Paying close attention to golden eagle?

parts.note: rapt means absorbed, fully attentive
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Someone watching intently as a golden eagle soars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word. 'golden eagle' reads as one bird, but 'golden' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle is an example of a bird of prey, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Undermined MP's excuse for not voting

definitions.meaning: a paired MP agrees with an opposing member that neither will vote

explanation.surface: A weakened politician explains why they missed a parliamentary vote.
explanation.walkthrough: In the UK Parliament, MPs of opposite parties can be 'paired' so both may miss a vote without changing the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Something weakened or damaged in function has been undermined; split differently the letters say I'M PAIRED.

clue.text: As classical art ruined Nice

parts.note: ars is Latin for art

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters of the town are broken up

explanation.surface: Like classical art destroyed in the French city of Nice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' looks like a link word but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: As is the chemical symbol for this poisonous element.

clue.text: As disused stations are covered by railway work

parts.note: abandoned stations end up covered in dust

explanation.surface: Abandoned railway stations lie under grime from the trains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link word; the long phrase gives IN DUST as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Industry means diligent labour, hard work, as in 'praised for her industry'.

clue.text: Head cold interrupting crazy rocker's comeback

indicators.note: a comeback turns the letters round, so they are read right to left
the answer breaks into the middle of these words, so its letters lie within them

explanation.surface: A sniffle disrupts an unhinged rock star's return to the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interrupting' signals letters inside 'crazy rocker', and 'comeback' says read them backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the medical term for acute inflammation of the nasal passages, the common cold.

clue.text: Electronics company has increased turnover after changing half its leaders

indicators.note: the leading letters of each word, starting from has through to its

explanation.surface: A firm boosts its sales after a boardroom shake-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its leaders' looks like the board, but 'leaders' means first letters of the seven words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a large Japanese electronics and engineering corporation.

clue.text: Hit friends back

indicators.note: back here means reversed, so the word for friends is read from its end

parts.note: pals are friends

explanation.surface: Someone strikes their friends in retaliation.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit with an open hand is a common synonym.

clue.text: Antibiotic fix covering nurse in charge getting sick

indicators.note: the fix word wraps around the other pieces, covering them

parts.note: to pin is to fix in place
EN is an enrolled nurse
ill means sick

explanation.surface: An ailing nurse who is in charge gets a dose of antibiotic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is a link word. 'fix' looks like a medical fix, but it supplies PIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleming's mould-derived drug was the first widely used antibiotic.

clue.text: Weapons indicating elms

parts.note: putting the letters L and M inside ES spells the word elms

explanation.surface: Weapons point to elm trees.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as instructions: L AND M IN ES, which builds E(LM)S.
explanation.definitionFit: Explosive devices buried in the ground are weapons.

clue.text: Fragrances pass over genders, oddly

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
O is over, from cricket scoring

indicators.note: taking the odd-numbered letters of genders

explanation.surface: Perfumes that ignore gender, oddly.
explanation.definitionFit: Eau de cologne is a light perfume, so these are scents.

clue.text: Choral rite oddly not expecting responses

indicators.note: arranged in an odd way, so the letters of the choral rite are scrambled

explanation.surface: A church choir's service in which nobody answers back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' is the anagram signal here, not a call for odd letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhetorical question is asked for effect, with no answer wanted.

clue.text: Park country's unfinished concert

parts.note: rec, a recreation ground, is a park

indicators.note: the country is left without its last letter

parts.note: Italy is the country

explanation.surface: A park in an unfinished state hosts a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a performance of music, often by a soloist.

clue.text: Woman from Clackmannan

indicators.note: the name is taken from within the letters of the place name

explanation.surface: A woman who comes from a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Clackmannan is a small town in central Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a common female first name, so it stands for a woman.

clue.text: You break records for chrysanthemums?

indicators.note: the U breaks into the records word, sitting inside it

parts.note: annals are historical records
U sounds like you, text-speak

explanation.surface: Someone smashes records for growing chrysanthemums.
explanation.definitionFit: Some chrysanthemums are plants that live just one year; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Artist comes in with an apparition

indicators.note: the artist enters the other word, going inside it

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter enters accompanied by a ghost.
explanation.definitionFit: A wraith is a ghost or spectral figure.

clue.text: Mad mother who has her child adopted?

definitions.text: mother who has her child adopted?
definitions.meaning: the bird of that name lays its eggs in other birds' nests for them to raise

explanation.surface: A mother who gives up her child for adoption is cruelly called crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird leaves its young for foster parents to rear; the same word is slang for crazy.

clue.text: Time for male to cross line

indicators.note: the line crosses into the male word, sitting inside it

parts.note: a cock is a male bird
L is line

explanation.surface: It is time for a man to step over the line.
explanation.definitionFit: To clock a time is to record it; as a noun it is a timepiece standing for time.

clue.text: A way mother fills up anorexic fielder

indicators.note: the road and mother go inside the word for anorexic, filling it

parts.note: anorexic means very thin
RD is road, a way
ma is mother

explanation.surface: Mother tries to feed up a painfully thin child.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a cricket fielding position behind the wicket on the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: The position names the player standing there, so it is a cricket fielder.

clue.text: Grass woodlanders up

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: deer live in woodland

explanation.surface: Forest folk are lifting up grass.
explanation.definitionFit: A reed is a tall grass-like plant of wetlands.

clue.text: Beats Turkey with lightweights

parts.note: TR is the international vehicle code for Turkey
ounces are small units of weight

explanation.surface: Turkey defeats a team of lightweight boxers.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce is to defeat soundly, so the verb means beats.

clue.text: Capital WW2 weapon Anne brought back

parts.note: the V1 flying bomb, written VI

indicators.note: brought back means turned round, so the name is reversed

parts.note: taken as written before reversal

explanation.surface: Anne brought a wartime weapon home with her.
explanation.walkthrough: The V1 'doodlebug' was a German flying bomb; the 1 is read as letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the capital city of Austria.

clue.text: Hollywood film with fish on inland beach

parts.note: Hollywood is in LA, Los Angeles
Kes is Ken Loach's 1969 film about a boy and a kestrel
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A Hollywood movie featuring fish is shot on a beach away from the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'on' are link words. Kes is a British film, so 'Hollywood film' splits in two.
explanation.definitionFit: The shore of a lake is a beach that lies inland.

clue.text: Writes on behalf of good MCs

parts.note: masters of ceremonies are hosts

explanation.surface: Skilled compères pen material for someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghostwriter writes books or speeches credited to another person.
